chunkInfo.content: Artificial Intelligence (AI): Introduction — Computer Fundamentals & Emerging Technologies — PYQDeck PyQdeck Logo PyQdeckBEU PYQ ArchiveSubjectsSyllabusBlog Home Syllabus Computer Fundamentals & Emerging Technologies Artificial Intelligence (AI): Introduction Emerging Technologies (8hrs) Computer Fundamentals & Emerging Technologies Artificial Intelligence (AI): Introduction Watch lectures Artificial Intelligence (AI): Introduction 1. Definition Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the branch of computer science that builds machines and software capable of performing tasks that normally require human intelligence — learning, reasoning, problem-solving, perception, understanding language and decision-making. John McCarthy, who coined the term, defined it as "the science and engineering of making intelligent machines". AI does not have to imitate a human brain; it only has to achieve a comparable outcome (acting rationally and effectively). Alan Turing's 1950 test — can a machine's conversation be indistinguishable from a human's? — gave the field its first operational benchmark.

Introduction to Artificial Intelligence (8hrs) Introduction to AI What is AI? Watch lectures What is AI? — Beginner-Friendly Notes 1. Simple Definition (remember this) Artificial Intelligence (AI) = making computers do things that normally need human intelligence — like seeing, understanding language, learning from experience, and making decisions. If a task needs you to think (not just calculate), and a machine can do it — that is AI. Beginner analogy: A calculator is not AI (it just follows fixed arithmetic rules). Google Maps suggesting a faster route by learning traffic patterns is AI (it learns and predicts). 2. What AI Is NOT Not magic, not a brain in a box — it is programs + data + mathematics. Not just robots — most AI has no body (search, recommendations, chat). Not always perfect — AI learns from data, so biased or small data → biased/wrong AI. 3. The 4 Ways People Define AI (Russell & Norvig) Textbooks frame AI in a 2×2 grid.

A Brief History 1950 Turing test → 1956 Dartmouth Conference (the term "Artificial Intelligence" is born) → 1960s-70s symbolic AI, search, game playing → 1970s-80s expert systems (MYCIN, DENDRAL) and the first AI winter → 1997 Deep Blue beats Kasparov → 2011 IBM Watson wins Jeopardy, Siri launches → 2012 AlexNet ignites deep learning (thanks to GPUs and big data) → 2016 AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol → 2017 the Transformer architecture → 2022+ generative AI (ChatGPT, diffusion image models) → today, multimodal and agentic AI. 3. Levels and Types of AI By capability Meaning Status Narrow / Weak AI Performs one specific task as well as or better than a human Exists today (search, translation, recommendations, chess, face unlock) General AI (AGI) Human-level ability across all cognitive tasks, transferring learning between domains Hypothetical — not achieved Super AI Far exceeds the best human minds in every field Speculative By functionality Meaning Reactive machines Respond to the current input only, no memory (Deep Blue, simple game AI) Limited memory Use recent past data (self-driving cars, chatbots) Theory of mind Model the beliefs and emotions of others — research stage Self-aware Conscious of itself — conceptual only 4.

chunkInfo.content: How to Spot an AI Problem (3 checks) Environment is uncertain / large (too many possibilities to hard-code) Needs learning or search (pattern from data, or exploring options) Needs human-like judgement (classify, predict, decide, generate) If all three are low, plain programming is enough — you don't need AI. 8. Common Mistakes Beginners Make Thinking AI = human consciousness — no, it is narrow task intelligence today. Thinking more data always helps — only clean, relevant data helps. Thinking AI writes its own goals — goals are still given by humans (PEAS in next topics). 9. One-Line Summary to Write in Exam AI is the study and design of intelligent agents — systems that perceive their environment and act to maximise their chance of achieving goals, exhibiting capabilities such as learning, reasoning, perception and language understanding. 10. Quick Self-Check Is a rule if temperature > 30 → turn on AC AI? (No — fixed rule, no learning/search) Is email spam detection AI? (Yes — learns patterns from examples) Name one AI you used today and which capability it used. answer.answerText:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a branch of computer science focused on building machines and software capable of performing tasks that typically require human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning, problem-solving, perception, and decision-making. John McCarthy, who coined the term, defined it as "the science and engineering of making intelligent machines". 

Rather than imitating the human brain, AI aims to achieve rational and effective outcomes. It can be defined as the study and design of intelligent agents that perceive their environment and act to maximize their chances of achieving goals. AI is not magic or a physical robot; it consists of programs, data, and mathematics.
